explanations.text:
The skill is the rulebook claude reads before it explains a code
file for you. Two loops run through it.

The everyday loop — one file, one abstraction:

    you: "how does server.py work?"
         claude reads the file and writes the abstraction
         for a reader who knows the subject, not the code
                                                          ([explain](2. Explain))
         every name in it is a pin to a real thing:
         a block of the file, an earlier abstraction,
         or another file of the project
                                                          ([anchors](1. Anchors))
         claude shows the text and stops.
    you: "map it"
         the tool checks the pins and adds one entry     ([map](3. Map))
         claude tells you what went in and what is still
         not covered                                     ([report](6. Report))
    you: paste a line back
         claude finds the abstraction it belongs to
                                      ([how you point](How the user points at things))
         and rewords it in place, or undoes the last one
                                            ([rewrite](4. Rewrite and rollback))

The training loop — one file, three abstractions, your pick:

    you: human train --open
         the rows you did not pick last time come along
    you: "how does server.py work?"
         claude writes three versions and gives them to
         the tool, one call each                           ([train](7. Train))
           best         the shape the catalog says
           refinement   that shape after your corrections;
                        for a changed file, the map's own text
           free         whatever helps you most
    you: "rewrite the refinement"
         claude hands the same slot in again; the last text stays
    you: open the feed, swipe, pick one per file,
         say why if you want
    you: human train --close
         the tool maps every pick itself.

When the code changes, both loops meet the same step: the tool
carries the pins to the new lines and claude mends only the words
that went untrue, once per change     ([sync](5. Sync after a change)).

What the skill is, in one line: claude abstracts, the tool maps,
and only the tool writes the maps            ([decompile](decompile)).
